subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Fitness Literacy I: Training Principles Without Body Metrics
title: Unit assessment: noticing capability change through what the learner can now do under transfer
focus: noticing capability change through what the learner can now do
essentialQuestion: What actually makes a body more capable, and how would I notice it?
privacySafeScenario: Design a four-week progression for one self-chosen capability and state how progress will be recognized through tasks the learner can perform — never through weight, size, body composition, or appearance.
studentTask: Learner works noticing capability change through what the learner can now do applied to the learner’s own real training week rather than to a worked example at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of noticing capability change through what the learner can now do degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds noticing capability change through what the learner can now do applied to the learner’s own real training week rather than to a worked example, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: The chosen capability may be endurance, strength, mobility, coordination, balance, or a functional task; a learner with a medical restriction designs the progression inside that restriction with guardian input.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of noticing capability change through what the learner can now do yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.

The chosen capability may be endurance, strength, mobility, coordination, balance, or a functional task; a learner with a medical restriction designs the progression inside that restriction with guardian input.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where noticing capability change through what the learner can now do shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
